Lesson 10.3 · 37 of 78 · 24 min · Verified 17 Jul 2026

Customers, households, businesses and related parties

After this lesson you can:
  • Model a customer separately from roles in a facility
  • Represent households, groups and business control
  • Aggregate exposure without unsafe record merging

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page
  1. A person is not an application
  2. Relationships change risk
  3. Identity resolution with governance
  4. Regulatory anchors
  5. Where this lives in LoanOS
  6. Knowledge check

1. A person is not an application

The stable customer record represents an individual or legal entity across time.

An application assigns roles — applicant, co-applicant, guarantor, beneficial owner, signatory — and a facility assigns obligors and security providers.

Keeping identity separate from role prevents duplicate KYC, broken exposure and contradictory communication preferences.

2. Relationships change risk

Household membership drives microfinance indebtedness and FOIR.

Business ownership and control drive beneficial-owner KYC and connected exposure.

Group/JLG membership creates joint-liability evidence.

Guarantors and co-borrowers require their own consent, documents, affordability treatment and signing journey.

3. Identity resolution with governance

Matching may use PAN, CKYC, phone, address or device, but a similarity is not permission to merge.

Specify candidate-match review, survivorship of fields, retained aliases, audit history and rollback.

Deceased-borrower, legal-heir and nominee flows must preserve both privacy and servicing continuity.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-KYC-2016 — CDD includes legal entities, beneficial ownership, risk categorisation and ongoing review.
  • DPDP-2023 — Party data and relationship processing require purpose, minimisation and rights handling.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Retrieval practice

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. Two customer records share an address and device. What is the safe action?

  1. Merge automatically
  2. Create a governed match candidate and retain evidence
  3. Delete the newer record
  4. Ignore the match
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. Signals support review; they do not prove identity or authorise an irreversible merge.
